card.title: Energy flow and the ten per cent law as a pyramid

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Green plants fix the Sun's energy and hand it up the food chain, but most of it is spent and lost as heat at every step — which is why a food chain can never be long.

figure.caption: Upright energy pyramid: each trophic level holds about a tenth of the energy below it.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Only about 10 % of the energy at one trophic level reaches the next;  GPP − R = NPP;  Eₙ = E₁(0.1)ⁿ⁻¹

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Lindeman's ten per cent law is an average for energy transfer between trophic levels, and the energy pyramid it draws is always upright.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The pyramid of biomass inverts in a pond where phytoplankton turn over fast, and the pyramid of number inverts under one tree hosting thousands of insects.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Producers 10 000 kJ → primary consumers 1 000 kJ → secondary consumers 100 kJ → tertiary consumers 10 kJ, nine tenths lost at each step.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Ten per cent is only an average (a transfer can reach twenty) and it applies to energy alone — nutrient cycles are closed loops while energy flow is one-way.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: NPP = GPP − R;  energy to the next level = NPP × 0.1, applied once per level ⇒ Eₙ = E₁(0.1)ⁿ⁻¹

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Draw the energy pyramid upright before writing anything; one line of Eₙ = E₁(0.1)ⁿ⁻¹ carries the method mark by itself.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Explain Lindeman's ten per cent law with a labelled energy pyramid and calculate the energy available at the third trophic level.
